name: CogniSim — master's thesis and 2026 analysis
oneLiner: LaTeX sources of a master's thesis on CogniSim, plus a 2026 audit of what underneath it has ceased to exist.
summary: `thesis/` holds the sources of a master's thesis (Warsaw University of Technology, EiTI) describing CogniSim — a multi-agent system on LLMs in which agents play the roles of a software organisation and act out {{term:safe}} and Scrum ceremonies. `docs/` holds six numbered studies from 2026 that check what of that thesis still stands up: a defect audit of the sources, an ecosystem deprecation audit, a migration mapping onto {{term:maf}}, the publication record, related work, and a stack audit of the successor platform. The most interesting decision is not about content but about epistemology: **every external claim carries a {{term:poziom|verification level}}** — primary-artefact, primary-page, secondary or unverified — because the documents were written in a sandbox that blocked `openai.com`, `learn.microsoft.com` and `scaledagile.com`, and rather than pass over that in silence the author marked every such gap in the text. Stage 0 of the roadmap is finished: 22 defects in the thesis fixed, the instrument taken from 63 errors down to zero, both checkers running in CI and in pre-commit. What is unfinished is what the degree actually rests on — the thesis still poses no research question and reports no measurement of its own. Two studies contain explicit self-corrections, because independent re-verification showed two conclusions to be wrong.
license: MIT at the root, `thesis/` under GPL-3.0, `thesis/eiti/` with no stated licence (third-party material)
tests: No unit tests, because there is no application code. Two checkers do the job of a suite: `check-latex-hygiene.py` (424 lines) gives 0 errors and 66 warnings, matching the committed `artifacts/01/hygiene-after.txt` exactly, and `check-doc-links.py` (227 lines) gives 0 findings across 23 Markdown files. Both were run again during this review.
ci: Five workflows: LaTeX hygiene and document links run exactly the same scripts as pre-commit, `secret-scan.yml` runs gitleaks on push, on PR and weekly, CodeQL analyses Python weekly, and `build-thesis-pdf.yml` is `workflow_dispatch` only and assembles the PDF through `xu-cheng/latex-action` with `-shell-escape`. {{term:dependabot}} watches the action versions monthly.

metrics.label: Size
metrics.value: 1,715 lines of .tex, 3,045 lines of Markdown, 847 lines of scripts

docs.label: Defect audit of the thesis sources

components.name: check-latex-hygiene.py
components.description: 424 lines of plain Python with no dependencies, catching defects a successful LaTeX build does not report: a bare `%` stuck to a word, a `\cite` with no entry, a duplicated bib key, a `\ref` with no `\label`, a backtick in typeset text, a Windows path in a listing. It masks the insides of `verbatim`/`lstlisting`/`minted` and the arguments of `\url` before it starts counting per cent signs.

components.name: check-doc-links.py
components.description: 227 lines checking that every relative link and every heading anchor in the Markdown set resolves. The second half enforces the ten required study sections in the order imposed by `architecture-standards`, so it carries over to this whole portfolio.

components.name: Runbook i skomitowane hooki
components.description: One command points `core.hooksPath` at the committed directory, and the pre-commit hook works on a snapshot from `git checkout-index`, not on the dirty working tree. `verify-secret-scan.sh` plants a key in a throwaway repository and checks that gitleaks actually fires.

components.name: Workflowy LaTeX-owe
components.description: Hygiene runs on a `thesis/**` path filter; the PDF build is manual and pulls in `py3-pygments` and `latexmk_shell_escape`, because without them chapter 4 does not typeset. Every workflow carries a comment at the top saying why it exists. Ready to graft into `llm-book` and `maf-book`.

components.name: Thesis sources
components.description: `main.tex` plus eight chapters and an appendix, the EiTI/PW class, 27 figures, 161 bibliography entries and two published conference papers as PDFs. The distribution of length says a lot: chapter 4 has 722 lines, chapter 6 has forty-one.

components.name: Studia badawcze
components.description: Six studies in a fixed question–method–evidence–threats format, every external claim tagged with a {{term:poziom|verification level}}. Two studies contain self-corrections written into the text rather than quietly patched away.

components.name: Analiza produktowa
components.description: `MARKET-ANALYSIS.md` takes apart the widely quoted figures about the agent market and shows which of them do not survive a check. `PRODUCT-NICHES.md` lists five niches and two traps, with a falsification condition attached to each recommendation.

components.name: Standards-compliance layer
components.description: P1–P15 and the REPO-BASELINE checklist answered for a repository with no application code, with five open gaps recorded rather than passed over. Gap G-5 says outright that this document once lied about itself.

overlaps.reason: This repository audits that platform in study 06 and cites it as the v2 reference architecture, but does not modify it — decision D-009 records the split explicitly.
The whole `docs/architecture/` layer measures this repository against that constitution, and `.claude/settings.json` declares its marketplace and three plugins.
Study 03 maps the thesis implementation onto {{term:maf}}, which is exactly the subject of that book. The migration table is publishable on its own.
Study 02 audits the LangChain and LangGraph 1.x deprecations on the same facts that book describes from the API side.
The same subject — multi-agent systems on LLMs — except there as a working experiment, and here as a degree thesis and its critique.

product: **No buyer** for the repository itself: it is a degree thesis plus its audit, so the value is academic and reputational. A buyer only appears in `docs/product/`, and concerns the successor platform rather than these documents — an {{term:rte}} or a transformation office paying for a dress rehearsal of PI Planning, sold through the {{term:spc}} consultant channel. The documents themselves do have two real channel uses: the LangChain 0.1 → Microsoft Agent Framework migration table is fit to publish on its own, and the study methodology with its verification levels is a better engineering calling card than most of the code in this portfolio.
highlights: The most frequently reported defect in the thesis — 22 unresolved citation keys in chapter 2 — **does not exist**. An independent recount gives 96 cited keys and all of them resolve to entries in the bibliography.

Study 03 proves from the repository, not from a blog, that the whole LangChain `cookbook/` directory — 106 files with the `DialogueAgent` and `DialogueSimulator` patterns that chapter 4 rests on — was deleted in commit `a4c8baeb` on 6 October 2025.

The secret-scan workflow does not only run gitleaks: it plants a key in a `minted` listing in a throwaway repository and fails the job if the scanner does not report it. A green result means the control **works**, not that it ran.

Two studies contain explicit self-corrections. Defects N3 and N4 were first recorded as non-reproducible, then found and corrected in the text, with a methodological conclusion: you look for a LaTeX defect by how it renders, not by how it was written.

`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` separates three provenances and says outright that 'Copyleft by …' in the EiTI class is a sentiment, not a licence, and that nothing in the repository extends any permission over those files.
gaps: **The thesis PDF has never once been built.** Every claim about how the document typesets is predicted from the sources, not observed (gap G-2). One run of `build-thesis-pdf.yml` closes it.
Stages 1–4 of the roadmap are only costed. The problem the degree actually rests on — no research question and no measurement of its own — is untouched, and stage 0 was about source hygiene.
Study 04 has draft status and will keep it until somebody reads the primary record: every identifier is a secondary source, and the audit itself caught one invented 2026 item.
A large share of the external claims rests on secondary sources, because the sandbox blocked the vendors' domains (gap G-3). The repository marks this but does not fix it.
`thesis/` can diverge from the author's copy on Overleaf and nothing detects it — {{term:drift}} that no checker sees (gap G-1).
risks: **Name collision:** `cognitive-multi-agent-simulation` and `cognitive-multi-agent-simulation-analysis` differ by one suffix, and they are two entirely different artefacts — a .NET platform against a thesis and its critique.

The MIT LICENSE header says 'Copyright (c) 2026 dev_insight' — that is the name of another project in the portfolio, not the author's name. A copied template undermines a file the rest of the repository treats very seriously.

`thesis/eiti/` is third-party material with no licence stated, and the two conference PDFs in `thesis/articles/` are author manuscripts included under the right to self-archive. The risk passes to anyone who copies those directories onward.
All 847 lines of Python and shell were written in one session, on the same day as the studies that use them as evidence. Study 01 itself lists this as a threat to validity.
next: Run `build-thesis-pdf.yml` once and read paragraph 6.1.2. It closes gap G-2 and confirms the fix for defect D1 — one click against the largest open debt.
Fix the copyright line in LICENSE to the actual rights holder. The same fault sits in at least two other repositories in the portfolio.
Look for the sixteen output directories from March 2024, visible in two screenshots in chapter 4. If they survived, an honest results chapter with a real n is days of work rather than weeks.
Read the study 04 identifiers from an unrestricted browser and move them from secondary to primary, or withdraw them — otherwise the document stays a draft permanently.
Add one sentence to chapter 5 saying that what is modelled is Core {{term:safe}} 6.0: PI Planning has been rebuilt, and Inspect and Adapt is being replaced.
headline: Stage 0 closed and measured; the thesis still has no research question
